purpose: Evaluate whether a clean foreground policy can reduce reference-background workload without suppressing labeled controlled attacks.
allowed_feature_sources: candidate native routing and weak-context fields
raw-derived community sidecar with join status
forbidden_policy_features: legacy final high needs low labels

evaluation_populations.active_attack: Rows or events with controlled active attack membership.
evaluation_populations.scenario_control: Injected stable or recovery controls, reported separately from attack truth.
evaluation_populations.hard_negative: Provenance-backed plausible non-attack lookalikes; not confirmed benign.
evaluation_populations.reference_background: Rows with no injected scenario membership; not confirmed benign.
evaluation_populations.mixed_membership: Rows containing both scenario and non-scenario members; excluded from pure background denominators and audited separately.

assignment_states.protected_foreground: Explicitly protected by the frozen clean foreground policy.
assignment_states.gray_retained: Not protected but retained because suppression is not justified.
assignment_states.operational_background_suppressed: Counterfactually suppressed from downstream workload; not a benign label.

feasibility_gates.interpretation: Engineering feasibility gates only; they are not paper-level low-false-positive claims.

uncertainty_reporting.small_scenario_rule: Report exact numerators and denominators; do not generalize from four attack scenarios.

hard_stop_if: truth or scenario metadata enters policy features
mixed-membership rows enter the pure reference-background denominator
evidence snapshots or provenance differ from the frozen full replay
do_not_proceed_if: reference background suppression rate is below 0.05
on_failure: report the first failing layer and reason
revise the policy without changing this evaluation denominator
rerun as a new protocol version

forbidden_claims: zero suppressed attacks proves real-world recall
poisoning or evasion robustness is proven
